draft.title: Gravity, mass and weight
card: Gravity is a pulling force between any two objects that have mass. The more mass an object has, the stronger its pull. Earth is so massive that its pull on us is easy to notice.
the amount of matter in an object. It is measured in kilograms (kg) and stays the same wherever the object is.
the force of a planet's gravity on an object. It is a force, so it is measured in newtons (N) and points down towards the centre of the planet.
The Moon has less mass than Earth, so its gravity is weaker. An astronaut has the same mass on the Moon as on Earth, but a smaller weight.
draft.remember: Mass is how much matter there is. Weight is the pull of gravity on it.

a.q: An astronaut travels from Earth to the Moon. What happens to her mass and her weight?
opts: Mass stays the same and weight gets smaller
Mass gets smaller and weight stays the same
Both mass and weight stay the same
Both mass and weight get smaller
a.why: Mass is the amount of matter in her body, and that does not change with place. Weight is the pull of gravity, and the Moon's pull is weaker than Earth's. Saying that both get smaller mixes up mass with weight.
a.clue: Which one depends on the pull of the planet?

b.q: Liam has a rock with a mass of 2 kg. He hangs it from a force meter on Earth, then takes it to the Moon. Which statement is correct?
opts: The reading is less on the Moon and the mass is still 2 kg
The reading is less on the Moon because the mass is smaller
The reading is the same on both because the mass is 2 kg
The reading is more on the Moon and the mass is still 2 kg
b.why: A force meter measures weight, which is the pull of gravity. The Moon's gravity is weaker, so the reading is smaller. The rock has the same amount of matter, so its mass stays 2 kg. The option saying the mass is smaller is tempting but confuses mass with weight.
b.clue: A force meter measures a force, not the amount of matter.

a.best: Mass stays the same and weight gets smaller

b.best: The reading is less on the Moon and the mass is still 2 kg

problems.detail: Weight is defined as 'the force of a planet's gravity' pointing 'towards the centre of the planet', but the card then applies weight to the Moon, which is not a planet. A Year 7 student could be confused about whether weight exists on the Moon. Use 'a planet's or moon's gravity' or 'the gravity of Earth, the Moon or another body'.
